            },
            {
              type: [32m'text'[39m,
              text: [32m'# Fleet Rollout Orchestration with Ash.Reactor\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Background\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`Orchestra` is an internal control plane that rolls new software out onto a fleet of edge nodes.\n'[39m +
                [32m'A rollout has to reserve capacity on every target node, obtain an approval, deploy to the nodes,\n'[39m +
                [32m'and — if anything goes wrong at any point — put the whole fleet back exactly the way it was.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The persistence layer is `Ash.DataLayer.Ets`, which has **no transactions**. Nothing can be\n'[39m +
                [32m'rolled back by the database: every reversal has to be performed explicitly by the workflow itself,\n'[39m +
                [32m'including reversing work that had already completed successfully when a *later* step failed.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Your job is to build the domain and the orchestration graph. Everything runs locally in this\n'[39m +
                [32m'container; there are no external services and no network access.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Build an Ash domain describing the fleet, and an `Ash.Reactor` workflow that orchestrates a\n'[39m +
                [32m'rollout end to end with correct failure, retry and rollback semantics, an observable execution\n'[39m +
                [32m'trace, and bounded parallelism.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The workflow must be able to:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'- reserve capacity on many nodes at once and fail cleanly when a node cannot supply it,\n'[39m +
                [32m'- branch on the size of the rollout to decide what kind of approval is required,\n'[39m +
                [32m'- deploy to the nodes with bounded parallelism, retrying an attempt that fails transiently,\n'[39m +
                [32m'- reverse *in-flight* work when an attempt fails, and reverse *already-completed* work when the\n'[39m +
                [32m'  rollout as a whole fails,\n'[39m +
                [32m'- and expose an ordered trace of what happened that an operator (and the tests) can inspect.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Implementation Hints\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'- Project path: `/home/user/orchestra`. The mix project, its pinned dependencies and\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `lib/orchestra/application.ex` already exist and are pre-compiled; there is no network access,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  so do not add dependencies. Elixir 1.18.4 / OTP 27.3.4, `ash` 3.31.0, `reactor` 1.0.5.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- The OTP application is `:orchestra` and `config/config.exs` already declares\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `config :orchestra, ash_domains: [Orchestra.Fleet]`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `mix compile` must succeed with no compilation errors.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Domain and resources\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Define the domain `Orchestra.Fleet` and five resources, all on `Ash.DataLayer.Ets`. Attribute\n'[39m +
                [32m'names, types and defaults are fixed because the tests read them directly:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`Orchestra.Fleet.Node`\n'[39m +
                [32m': `id` (uuid primary key), `name` (`:string`), `region` (`:atom`, one of `:us_east`, `:eu_west`,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `:ap_south`), `slots_total` (`:integer`), `slots_used` (`:integer`, default `0`), `state`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  (`:atom`, one of `:idle`, `:reserved`, `:live`, default `:idle`), `deploy_failures_remaining`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  (`:integer`, default `0`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`Orchestra.Fleet.Rollout`\n'[39m +
                [32m': `id` (uuid primary key), `name` (`:string`), `strategy` (`:atom`, one of `:canary`, `:blast`),\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `status` (`:atom`, one of `:pending`, `:running`, `:succeeded`, `:rolled_back`, default\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `:pending`), `deployed_node_count` (`:integer`, default `0`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`Orchestra.Fleet.Placement`\n'[39m +
                [32m': `id` (uuid primary key), `rollout_id` (`:uuid`), `node_name` (`:string`), `slots` (`:integer`),\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `status` (`:atom`, one of `:reserved`, `:deploying`, `:deployed`, `:released`, default\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `:reserved`), `attempts` (`:integer`, default `0`), `compensations` (`:integer`, default `0`),\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `undos` (`:integer`, default `0`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`Orchestra.Fleet.Approval`\n'[39m +
                [32m': `id` (uuid primary key), `rollout_id` (`:uuid`), `level` (`:atom`, one of `:auto`, `:board`),\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `slots` (`:integer`), `status` (`:atom`, one of `:granted`, `:revoked`, default `:granted`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`Orchestra.Fleet.Lease`\n'[39m +
                [32m': `id` (uuid primary key), `rollout_name` (`:string`), `status` (`:atom`, one of `:held`,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `:released`, default `:held`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The domain must expose exactly these code-interface functions (bang variants included):\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `Orchestra.Fleet.register_node/3` — positional args `name`, `region`, `slots_total`; the\n'[39m +
                [32m'  optional params map may additionally carry `deploy_failures_remaining`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `Orchestra.Fleet.get_node/1` — fetch a single node by `name`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `Orchestra.Fleet.list_nodes/0`, `Orchestra.Fleet.list_rollouts/0`,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `Orchestra.Fleet.list_placements/0`, `Orchestra.Fleet.list_approvals/0`,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `Orchestra.Fleet.list_leases/0` — read every record of that resource.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `Orchestra.Fleet.plan_rollout/1` — a **generic action** taking one argument `targets`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  (`{:array, :map}`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`plan_rollout/1` returns `{:ok, %{total_slots: integer, node_names: [String.t()],\n'[39m +
                [32m'target_count: integer}}` where `node_names` is sorted ascending. It must instead return\n'[39m +
                [32m'`{:error, %Ash.Error.Invalid{}}` whose `errors` list contains an\n'[39m +
                [32m"`%Ash.Error.Action.InvalidArgument{field: :targets}` when `targets` is empty, when any element's\n"[39m +
                [32m'`slots` is not a positive integer, or when a node name appears more than once.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### The workflow\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`Orchestra.Rollout.Reactor` is executed by the tests as\n'[39m +
                [32m'`Reactor.run(Orchestra.Rollout.Reactor, inputs)` where `inputs` is a map with exactly the keys\n'[39m +
                [32m'`:rollout_name` (`String.t()`), `:strategy` (`:canary` or `:blast`), `:targets` and\n'[39m +
                [32m'`:board_threshold` (integer). `:targets` is an ordered list of maps with the atom keys\n'[39m +
                [32m'`:node_name` (`String.t()`) and `:slots` (positive integer).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'On success it must return `{:ok, result}` where `result` is a map with exactly the keys\n'[39m +
                [32m"`:rollout_id` (the created rollout's id), `:status` (always `:succeeded`), `:deployed_nodes`\n"[39m +
                [32m'(the target node names, sorted ascending), `:total_slots`, `:approval_level` (`:auto` or\n'[39m +
                [32m'`:board`) and `:summary`. `:summary` must equal, with no leading or trailing whitespace:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'Rollout <rollout_name> deployed <target count> node(s) in <strategy> mode with <approval level> approval.\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'On any failure it must return an `{:error, _}` tuple.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Observable behaviour the tests rely on:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'1. Exactly one `Lease` is created per run, with `rollout_name` set from the input. Whatever\n'[39m +
                [32m'   happens, by the time the run returns its `status` is `:released`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'2. Exactly one `Rollout` is created per run, with `name` and `strategy` from the input. On\n'[39m +
                [32m'   success it ends as `status: :succeeded` with `deployed_node_count` equal to the number of\n'[39m +
                [32m'   targets. On failure it ends as `status: :rolled_back` with `deployed_node_count` `0`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"3. For every target, capacity is reserved on the named node: the node's `slots_used` grows by the\n"[39m +
                [32m"   target's `slots` and its `state` becomes `:reserved`, and one `Placement` is created carrying\n"[39m +
                [32m"   the rollout's id, the node name and the slot count. Reserving more slots than a node has free\n"[39m +
                [32m'   (`slots_used + slots > slots_total`) must fail the run, and so must naming a node that does\n'[39m +
                [32m'   not exist. Reservations are not retried.\n'[39m +
                [32m'4. No deployment may begin until every reservation has succeeded.\n'[39m +
                [32m"5. Exactly one `Approval` is created per run, carrying the rollout's id and `slots` equal to the\n"[39m +
                [32m'   total slot count. Its `level` is `:board` when the total slot count is greater than or equal\n'[39m +
                [32m'   to `:board_threshold`, and `:auto` otherwise. On success it ends `:granted`; if the rollout\n'[39m +
                [32m'   fails it ends `:revoked`. The approval must be produced by a **separate, independently\n'[39m +
                [32m'   runnable** reactor `Orchestra.Rollout.ApprovalReactor`, which the tests also execute directly\n'[39m +
                [32m'   as `Reactor.run(Orchestra.Rollout.ApprovalReactor, %{rollout_id: id, total_slots: n,\n'[39m +
                [32m'   board_threshold: t})` and which must return `{:ok, %Orchestra.Fleet.Approval{}}`. That\n'[39m +
                [32m"   reactor must choose the level with Reactor's `switch` step.\n"[39m +
                [32m'6. Deploying one target is the responsibility of `Orchestra.Rollout.Steps.DeployNode`, a module\n'[39m +
                [32m'   implementing the `Reactor.Step` behaviour with `run/3`, `compensate/4` and `undo/4`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"7. Every deployment attempt takes at least 50 ms of wall-clock time, raises the target's\n"[39m +
                [32m'   `Placement.attempts` by one and sets its `status` to `:deploying`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"8. An attempt fails if and only if the node's `deploy_failures_remaining` is greater than `0`\n"[39m +
                [32m'   when the attempt begins; a failing attempt reduces `deploy_failures_remaining` by one.\n'[39m +
                [32m'   A successful attempt sets the placement `status` to `:deployed` and the node `state` to\n'[39m +
                [32m'   `:live`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"9. A failed attempt is compensated: the placement's `compensations` rises by one and its `status`\n"[39m +
                [32m'   returns to `:reserved`. The deployment is then retried, but a target is attempted **at most\n'[39m +
                [32m'   four times in total**; a node whose `deploy_failures_remaining` is `3` therefore ends up\n'[39m +
                [32m'   deployed, while `4` fails the run.\n'[39m +
                [32m'10. When the run fails, everything already done must be undone. Each placement whose deployment\n'[39m +
                [32m'    had succeeded gets `undos` raised by one and `status` set to `:released` — a placement that\n'[39m +
                [32m"    never deployed successfully keeps `undos` at `0`. Every reservation is reversed: the node's\n"[39m +
                [32m'    `slots_used` returns to its previous value and, once it reaches `0`, its `state` returns to\n'[39m +
                [32m'    `:idle`. Placement rows are never deleted.\n'[39m +
                [32m'11. Rollback of completed work only starts once the failing target has used up its attempts.\n'[39m +
                [32m'12. At most two deployments may be in flight at any instant, and the workflow must actually use\n'[39m +
                [32m'    that budget: with six targets the tests require the maximum observed overlap to be exactly\n'[39m +
                [32m'    two.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Structure the tests introspect\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The tests read the reactor back with `Reactor.Info` and walk its steps, including nested ones.\n'[39m +
                [32m'The following must hold:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"- All resource work other than deploying an individual node is carried out by `Ash.Reactor`'s\n"[39m +
                [32m'  resource-action step types rather than by calling Ash from inside plain step code: the reactor\n'[39m +
                [32m'  must contain at least one create step, one update step, one read step and one generic-action\n'[39m +
                [32m'  step.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- The targets are iterated with a map step, and `Orchestra.Rollout.ApprovalReactor` is embedded\n'[39m +
                [32m'  with a compose step.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `Orchestra.Rollout.ApprovalReactor` picks the approval level with a switch step.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### The trace\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`Orchestra.Rollout.Trace` must expose `reset/0` (clears the trace and returns `:ok`) and\n'[39m +
                [32m'`entries/0`, which returns the recorded entries **in the order they were recorded** as a list of\n'[39m +
                [32m'`{event :: atom, label :: String.t()}` tuples. It must be usable from any process, including the\n'[39m +
                [32m'processes Reactor spawns for asynchronous steps, and it must be running as soon as the\n'[39m +
                [32m'application has started.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent can analyze code and create review comments on specific lines.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "review the code in src/auth"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "add review comments to this file"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the globFiles tool instead, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the readFile tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Other tasks that are not related to the agent descriptions above\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Launch multiple agents tools concurrently whenever possible to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
